theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Energy (+0.52%) and Financials (+0.46%) led the market today, while Technology (-1.45%) and Consumer Discretionary (-0.38%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -0.49% versus +0.07% for defensives and +0.16% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -0.37%, Dow -0.30%, Nasdaq -0.73% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -0.69%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 2.31% to 19.46, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold slipped 2.03% to $4,041.00, crude oil was little changed at $86.32, and bitcoin slipped 0.41% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
